articleTitle: The effect of random amplitude and phase errors on phased arrays performance
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, the effect of amplitude and phase errors as well as amplifiers and phase shifters failures on a phased array performance is investigated. It is found that random phase errors and phase shifters failures are dominant factors, they influence the peak sidelobe level, pointing angle accuracy, directive power and the half power beamwidth.

articleTitle: Implementation of linear phased arrays using dual mode horns
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: New method is applied on linear phased array in order to increase the inter-element separation. The method is based on using elements of scan capability, where the element pattern has a null at specified direction. Dual mode horns are used here, where the position of the element pattern null is controlled by the relative amplitude and phase of the second mode. In this case if the element pattern null is in the same position of a grating lobe it can eliminate it. Consequently, one can double the inter-element spacing used in common linear array without any grating lobes in the scan region.

articleTitle: Comparison of multibeam receive antenna configurations for EHF satellite communications
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Reflector configurations suitable for a multibeam EHF satellite communication receive antenna are reviewed in this paper. Four different antenna systems have been studied and their relative performances are compared. Computer simulations have been performed to analyze the co-polar and cross-polar gain contours of the antennas and the results are discussed.

articleTitle: A modular analysis of electromagnetic scattering off large planar objects
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The modular approach to scattering is designed to facilitate the computation of complex problems in a gradual manner, resolving them into a series of sub-problems. In addition to the “Add-On” method [1-4], described earlier by the author, we introduce the following two modular schemes: 1. A rapid computation of different incident fields in the Conjugate Gradient context, where a basis of incident fields or currents is used to generate any incident field in an economical way; 2. A numerical Green's function pre-computation for an aperture in a large finite screen.

articleTitle: A novel printed antenna suitable for MMIC phased arrays
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microstrip antennas are inherently narrowband due to the resonant nature of the top and bottom metal plates. Their typical bandwidths are between 0.1 to 3 %, although this can be improved somewhat by increasing the thickness of the substrate. However, if one intends to integrate MMIC circuitry and microstrip antennas onto the same substrate for phased array applications, the thickness and material type of the substrate is fixed. Putting an airgap between the patch and the high dielectric constant substrate can also increase the bandwidth of the antenna by a certain amount, but if one raises the entire metal patch above the dielectric substrate the advantage of a planar fabrication process is lost. This paper describes a novel type of printed antenna which achieves a height increase by putting an airgap between the microstrip antenna and its substrate while maintaining compatibility with MMIC processing. Antennas were fabricated and measured at 14 GHz, and the results are compared with a rectangular solid patch printed on a standard MMIC GaAs substrate, (∊r=12.9). A microstrip patch on quartz (∊r=3.78), is also fabricated and measured as a reference.

articleTitle: A new method for null steering by element position perturbations
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Null steering methods usually involve costly and complicated amplitude and/or phase control systems. A new technique is presented for null steering based on the element positions perturbations. This method possesses an even symmetry pattern cancellation, which allows nulls to be imposed at symmetrical positions around the main beam. Also it frees the phase shifters to be used solely for steering the main beam towards the direction of the desired signal.

articleTitle: Unsymmetrical cylindrical dipole. analysis by moment method
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, after an overview of Moment Method, a cylindrical dipole with arbitrary feed location and arbitrary diameter is analysed. Elements of impedance matrix are formulated with piecewise linear and piecewise sinusoid functions, in a Galerkin procedure. Thereafter current distribution and input impedance of the antenna are computed. Numerical results are in agreement with variational solution [1], and measurments carried out by Brown and Woodward [2].

articleTitle: Scattering from conductors partially coated by thin materials
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Electromagnetic scattering from axisymmetric conducting bodies partially coated by thin materials is computed numerically. The formulation of the problem is based on an existing formula for a completely coated object. This formulation is valid as the coating thickness approaches zero. Other existing implementations fail to obtain correct results in this case. Numerous examples are considered. The numerical solution is verified by comparison with the exact solution for a sphere.

articleTitle: Effects of pre-comparator unbalance in radar antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The performance of an amplitude sensing monopulse radar is largely affected by the hardware imperfections of the receiver. This paper describes an analysis on the effects of the pre-comparator phase and amplitude unbalance on the radar antenna. In this paper an anlaytical antenna model is used, the radiation patterns of the two squinted beams of the monopulse are represented by the Gaussian function. The sum and difference patterns are formed by the addition and subtraction of the two squinted beams, with the pre-comparator phase and amplitude unbalance included in the model. The discriminator curve obtained from the difference-divided-by-sum will then be an expression of the phase and amplitude unbalance. It is concluded from the analysis that the pre-comparator unbalance is insensitive to the post-comparator magnitude calibration. The effect of the phase unbalance on the boresight error is also summarised and presented in graphical form.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit of small receiving antennas in near field
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A rigorous analytical formulation of integral equations is presented for two classes of sensors. The source region Green's function affecting these integral equations is determined. Impedance boundary conditions are introduced to facilitate solutions of integral equations. Sensors are analyzed for the receiving mode in terms of the magnetic and electric effective lengths.

articleTitle: Dispersion characteristics of wide slotlines on thin dielectric substrates in a two dimensional phased array environment
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Constant width slot antennas(CWSA) and various types of tappered slot antennas(TSA) have attractive features like ease of construction, compatibility with MIC/MMIC technologies, Wider bandwidth,… for focal plane and phased array applications. Radiation and input circuit characteristics of a single isolated TSA/CWSA element has been investigated by several workers, but there are relatively few published works dealing with its behaviour in an array. The reports reflecting recent progresses in TSA array or subarray technology, for example, very interesting review of current art presented in(1) have based their studies on single element characteristics. Interaction between neighboring elements especially when the spacing between them is less than half a wavelength, has significant effects on element characteristics and the array as a whole. Important parameters such as pattern shape, beamwidth, bandwidth, S.L.L, directivity, and gain are quite sensitive to small variations in propagation constant along the antenna (2),(3). Consequently the knowledge of this parameter or equivalently the guided wavelength as a function of frequency and the other physical parameters of a uniform(CWSA) or nonuniform(TSA) structure in an array configuration is crucial for theoretical prediction of the system performances. For this purpose, mutual effects which are not fully understood yet should be taken into account properly.

articleTitle: TE scattering by a homogeneous elliptic cylinder coated by a dielectric and/or magnetic material
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The scattering properties of a homogeneous elliptic cylinder with a dielectric or magnetic coating are investigated analytically. The method of separation of variables is used to determine, exactly, the field distributions in each region for the transverse electric (TE) excitation. The technique can be easily extended to handle any number of layers. The behavior of the scattered field in the far zone is illustrated with numerical results for different core and coating material types, axial ratios, and electrical sizes.

articleTitle: The development of a SPICE model to predict the cross-talk reduction of coupled lines
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In high speed and wideband electronic circuit applications, it is desirable to minimize the cross-talk between parallel tracks on the printed circuit board. This paper presents a technique using vias, with which the cross-talk can be reduced by 50 to 90%. A SPICE model combined with the finite element method is developed to predict the performance and is validated with experimental results.

articleTitle: Input impedance and bandwidth of biconical microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A theoretical study is presented of the input impedance and bandwidth of biconical microstrip antennas asymmetrically excited by a coaxial probe feed. The antenna consists of a conducting cone cap on a grounded cone separated by an electrically thin dielectric. The structure is of biconical type. The analytic results for zero order modes (including the special case, TEM mode) of the biconical structure have been published in numerous papers and books [1,2]. The study of the φ dependent eigenvalues v of the spherical wave functions in the θ direction is published in [3]. It is found that there is a unique nontrivial eigenvalue for each TE mode and for the TM modes all eigenvalues are integer less than the order m, which are trivial solutions. The eigenvalues, v, for the proposed antenna structure are shown in Fig.2. The structure is modeled as a biconical cavity in spherical coordinate system. It is found that the dominant mode is the TE type, which is φ — dependent, and radiates in the broadside direction. The theoretical input impedance and bandwidth for different grounded cone angles are presented in this paper. The theoretical analysis of the conical microstrip antenna, the special case of these antennas, where the grounded cone becomes a plane, predicts that their bandwidth is wider than that of similar size planar circular disc antennas.

articleTitle: Current distributions and far field radiated by an arbitrary shape large bandwidth microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: It is well known that the bandwidth of a microstrip antenna can be increased by overlaying a parasitic element or director. A radioelectric model was presented [l] to explain this property in the case of a rectangular patch antenna. The purpose of this communication is a generalization of the analysis for an arbitrary shape symmetrical patch antenna coupled with a director. A quasi TEM two coupled transmission lines model is used to express the conduction and polarization current distributions and then the radiation patterns of an arbitrary-shape symmetrical patch coupled with a director and acting in a large bandwidth. In the particular case of the circular shape, theoretical results are in good agreement with experiments. The whole paper summarizes a recent thesis [2].

articleTitle: Design of an adaptive polarization antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes how an optimal target discrimination in a noisy environment can be obtained by an array antenna of angular beam steering and polarization agility. Results are proposed for a linear array of N elements spaced by a distance λ/2.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of a linear array antenna for a ground-wave radar at a coastal site
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The moment method is used to calculate the radiation pattern of a linear array for a number of array element configurations which include single monopole whips, single diamond shaped monopoles and three-element Yagi monopole whips over a perfect ground plane. Investigation of the far field radiation pattern is carried out for the cases of main lobe steering and pattern shaping (using Tschebyscheff polynomial). The effect of varying the frequency on the radiation pattern is also studied. Results show that the linear array with Yagi monopole elements has larger gain and less reception from high altitudes than the linear array with quarter-wavelength monopole whips. Diamond-shaped monopoles have wider frequency band than the single whips, and their individual pattern may help suppress grating lobes in some higher frequency ranges.

articleTitle: Window coupled waveguide bandpass filters
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Mode matching method is used to design window coupled waveguide microwave filters. The improvement is evident over conventional designs in which analytic models were used for tunable filters at lover frequencies. The particular choice of matrix representation and the family of modes help simplify the design process and reduce computer time. Measurements made with a bandpass filter, designed to operate at 15 GHz, show excellent agreement with theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Time-domain field response of a dielectric cylinder excited by a line source
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In the last decade, considerable attention has been devoted to the analysis of time-domain electromagnetic scattering problems. The time-domain current and field response of a circular cylinder to a plane electromagnetic wave has been already studied by many researchers [1]-[4]. Recently, the transient response of a conducting cylinder to a cylindrical electromagnetic wave has also been studied by the authors [5]-[7]. The purpose of the present paper is to derive analytical expressions of the time-domain field response of a dielectric circular cylinder to a cylindrical electromagnetic wave generated by a parallel filament carrying a unit-step current. The mathematical technique employed here is similar to that in [7]. The time-domain expression of the electric field is obtained by the inverse Laplace transform of the frequency-domain eigenfunction solution. The response contains contributions of the branch cut integrals and residues corresponding to appropriately chosen integration contours.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling effects of skewed microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Effects of mutual coupling in arrays of printed strip dipoles and rectangular microstrip antenna, and the mutual impedance effects for two printed dipoles in broadside, collinear and echelon arrangement have been reported in the literature. In this paper, the authors consider the case of skewed microstrip antennas. This initial study is to help analyze a circular arrangement of N patches with arbitrary angle of separation, shape, and excitation to allow greater directional control of the radiation pattern. For this study, two identical rectangular patches are considered. The theoretical input impedance and mutual coupling are obtained through the method of moments. The patches are fabricated on RT Duroid substrates having relative permittivities of 2.2 and 2.33 and a substrate thickness of 0.0787 cm. The measured values for the return loss and insertion loss as a function of the skew angle at the X band are presented. The measurements are conducted using an HP8408A network analyzer controlled by an HP85 personal computer. A comparison of the theoretical and experimental results is presented.

articleTitle: The effect of temperature and error tolerances on the performance of MLS array antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Microwave Landing System (MLS) has been demonstrated to be a highly precise guidance system and it is expected to replace the Instrument Landing System (ILS) in Canada and worldwide within this decade as a precision landing approach to aircrafts. Errors, however, caused by equipment imperfections and propagation effects are introduced in the course of generating and detecting the MLS guidance information. It is necessary to determine these errors as they are essential in designing and influencing the construction tolerances that determine the overall cost and performance of MLS antenna.

articleTitle: Time domain solution of half space problems
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Transmission-Line Matrix (TLM) method, originated by Johns and Beurle [1] is based on equivalent circuit models of Maxwell's equations and has been used extensively to analyze electromagnetic field problems [2]. In this paper the application of the TLM method to the simulation of radiation and scattering problems, in which there is a plane interface separating two infinite homogeneous media, is presented.

articleTitle: Transmission and reflection of electromagnetic waves from an inhomogeneous dielectric slab
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The reflected and transmitted field vectors resulting from an arbitrarily incident electromagnetic wave on a slab of an inhomogeneous dielectric are rigorously derived. The incident wave is expressed as a spectrum of infinite number of plane waves of different amplitude and phase. The slab is bounded between the two planes z=0 and z=d and the dielectric material is characterized by μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and ∊ where ∊ is proportional to l+pz while p is an arbitrary constant. Expressions for the electric and magnetic field vectors in the dielectric layer are found by solving the wave equation using separation of variables and power series techniques. The reflected and transmitted field vectors are then determined by the enforcement of the boundary conditions at the boundaries z=0 and z=d. Numerical results for thspecial case of an incident plane wave are presented.

articleTitle: Multipactor detection by resonant ring technique
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microwave components carrying medium or high powers in the space environment may suffer from multipactor breakdown. The resulting discharge can seriously affect the performance of communications equipment, so effective multipactor detection is essential in the development and qualification stages of flight hardware. This paper presents an extremely sensitive method of detection by means of a travelling wave resonant ring which provides high power levels without the need for costly high power amplifiers. The principle of the ring is presented together with design examples for systems at C-band and Ku-band frequencies presently in use at Spar Aerospace. Measured results on a variety of components are reported together with examples of induced multipactor which demonstrate the effectiveness of the ring technique.

articleTitle: Enhanced precision microstrip antenna measurements using a “Thru-Reflect-Line” calibration of a non-standard microstrip line at an arbitrary reference plane
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, an enhanced precision “Thru-Reflect-Line” (TRL) calibration technique is presented which allows highly accurate, de-embedded measurements to be made for a microstrip line-fed patch antenna with an arbitrary feed line characteristic impedance. This technique provides tremendous design flexibility and reduces the phase uncertainty to about 1 degree for the low dielectric constant material up to X-band frequency. An S-band example is provided.

articleTitle: A modal solution for the TE-mode resonances in a dielectric resonator on a grounded substrate
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Dielectric resonator are high permittivity ceramic structures which couple easily into planar and waveguide circuits. One of their more practical uses is in realizing high Q tuned circuits on planar microwave circuits. For such applications the important resonator parameters are, the resonant frequency, the Q of the mode and the coupling coefficients, among others. Most of the work in the past on this problem has concentrated primarily with the fundamental mode, the so called TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</inf> mode, and, in addition, has only concerned itself with the fields inside the resonator. They do not consider the influence of external structures such as the substrate and tuning plates. In modern filter design, however, one requires knowledge of not only the resonant frequency of the resonator, but also the fields around the device so that coupling and Q information can be determined. In this paper a method is developed that allows for the calculation of the resonant frequency of the TE modes, as well as the fields in all regions.

articleTitle: Mobile antenna diversity for cellular radio
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: With the advent of digital cellular radio, interest has been renewed in the area of mobile antenna diversity. This paper presents the results of experiments performed at NovAtel investigating the improvement in audio quality of typical cellular calls due to space diversity with a simple combining scheme.

articleTitle: CAD of patch subarrays for spaceborne X-SAR
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: French spatial agency (CNES) prepares for the end of the century, an X-Band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) called “Radar 2000”. Its mission is earth observation and vegetation control. Better than optical Spot satellites, it also provides supervision missions even with bad weather conditions.

articleTitle: A multipole expansion model for compact ferrous object detection
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Location and identification of compact ferrous objects is of major concern for detection of vehicles, submarines, achaeological objects, buried or hidden explosive objects, geological ore inclusions and inclusions in the human body. In principle, measurement of the spatial variation of the magnetostatic field associated with a compact ferrous object may be used to locate and identify the object and considerable success has been achieved in this area [1].

articleTitle: Radiation from an antenna near an arbitrarily shaped resistive sheet
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The radiation characteristics of a wire antenna located near an arbitrarily shaped resistive sheet are investigated, A triangular surface patch model is used for both the resistive sheet and the wire antenna. The investigation focusses primarily on the suitability of the resistive sheet model for representing thick, lossy dielectrics.

articleTitle: Scattering by a system of dielectric spheres
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The problem of multiple scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave incident on N dielectric spheres is investigated by two methods. The first is based on the multipole expansion method which gives analytic solution by using the spherical vector addition theorem to impose the boundary condition, while the second is an approximate method valid for relatively small spheres. Expressions for the total scattered field are obtained, from which the backscattering and bistatic cross sections can be determined.

articleTitle: A single-layered circularly-polarized radial line slot antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A radial line slot antenna (RLSA) is a kind of slotted waveguide array for DBS reception [1][2]. It is free of conductor loss and the aperture efficiency is more than 75%, twice as high as conventional planar antennas [3]. Those performances have been realized for double-layered RLSAs with uniform slot length.

articleTitle: Low angle radiation from HF antennas
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The influence of the ground on the fields of antennas has been discussed sporadically in the literature for many years. In most propagation calculations, it is assumed that the transmitting antenna has a fixed di-pole moment and the ground is taken to be a perfect conductor or possibly a homogeneous imperfectly conducting half-space. In practice, however, some kind of ground system is employed. Usually this takes the form of a metal screen or radial wire system which is on the surface of the ground, above it, or lightly buried. The design of such systems has been typically empirical. Apparently, the first analytical approach was carried out by Brown et a 1 [1]. Later works [2, 3] have dealt mainly with the influence of the ground system on the impedance. In most cases, it has been assumed that the radiated field, for a given current, was not appreciably inflenced by the presence of the ground screen. Infact, an analysis was presented previously by Wait and Pope[4] which is suitable for estimating the dependence of the ground wave on the size of a circular ground screen. Caleulations[5]based on this work supported the contention that a screen has only a small effect on the radiated field provided the radius of the screen is of the order of a wavelength or less. Very similar conclusion have been arrived at by British workers [6,7].

articleTitle: Analysis of planar microstrip structures of arbitrary shape — To be, or not to be in the spectral domain?
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The spectral domain Galerkin approach has mostly been used in conjunction with entire-domain basis functions. Occasionally, subsectional expansion functions defined over rectangular domains have also been employed. However, a rectangular mesh is not suitable for modeling microstrip structures having arbitrary or irregular shapes, which are more readily approximated in terms of triangular elements. Therefore, in this paper we explore the feasibility of using the spectral domain Galerkin method in conjunction with vector basis functions defined over triangular subdomains, such as those commonly used in the space domain approach based on the mixed-potential integral equation.

articleTitle: Automated antenna test range for small antennas
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: During the past two years the Antennas/Propagation group at NovAtel Communications Ltd has developed a unique automated Antenna Test Range (ATR). This facility is capable of measuring the entire far field radiation pattern of small antennas and displaying the results in two and three dimensional polar plots. This is accomplished by connecting a battery powered transmitter to the Antenna Under Test (AUT) and rotating it about two orthogonal axes. The emitted radiation is sampled over a spherical surface centered about the AUT. The manner in which the measurements are taken permits the hardware for the ATR to be fairly simple and inexpensive, while the software required to gather and process the data is fairly complex. Using this facility NovAtel is able to research and develop unique antennas for future products such as handheld cellular telephones and Global Positioning Systems. This paper presents a general description of the facility's operation and typical test results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave scattering from an infinite conducting fence
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic wave scattering from a infinite array constituted by wires with finite length is analysed by using a moment method and Floquet's theorem. When the period of the grating is far greater than the length of each wire, the numerical results are in good agreement with that for a single wire. Some numerical results for different periods and incident angles are presented.

articleTitle: An antenna pattern measurement technique for eliminating the fields scattered from a finite ground plane
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: When making ground plane based antenna pattern measurements in small anechoic chambers or compact ranges one is often restricted to a ground plane which is only a few wavelengths in extent. The fields scattered from the edges of this finite ground plane interfere with the fields radiated by the antenna, and are usually apparent in the radiation pattern as scalloping on the frontside of the pattern, and as spurious lobes on the backside. These features are not present in a theoretical analysis which assumes an infinite ground plane, and therefore make it difficult to compare theoretical field patterns with those measured experimentally. Previous investigators have made attempts to reduce the edge effects, with only moderate success [1,2]. Time gating (the technique of placing a temporal window filter around the desired signal) is effective at eliminating edge diffraction for relatively broadband antennas, near the zenith, where adequate temporal resolution is obtained. However, away from zenith, and for narrow band antennas, the diffracted and desired signals overlap, thus making time gating ineffective [3,4].

articleTitle: Phase center diversity antenna for resistance to multipath effects
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A concept/technique is described for reducing the effects of multipath contamination of the main beam, by using antenna phase center diversity. Results of a concept validation test are given.

articleTitle: Integrated antenna design using Resonant Tunneling Diodes
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Integrated antenna design utilizing Resonant Tunneling Diodes (RTDs) as the active element is described, where the intent is to integrate RTDs with printed microstrip dipoles on GaAs substrates for operation at mm-wave frequencies. RTDs are capable of operation at frequencies of up to 200 GHz, making them a good candidate for use as a mm-wave source. Issues involved in RTD and dipole modelling are first outlined, followed by considerations in integrated antenna simulation and design. A new state space modelling approach has been developed for RTD simulation, while a full wave discrete image technique is employed in dipole modelling. Small-signal equivalent circuits for both RTD and dipole antenna result, allowing for the formulation of an overall circuit model to describe the integrated antenna.

articleTitle: Real time modelling of HF radar for target detection
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A simple technique is being developed for real time High Frequency (HF) radar target detection. At present, models have been developed to extract ocean currents and wave height spectra from the Power Spectral Density Function (PSDF) of the HF radar data. The author is primarily concerned with the reduction of ocean clutter to improve target detection. The model for the ocean clutter data being considered is that of discrete sinusoids, whose phase velocities vary in time in a non-random fashion, as some function of the ocean spectra. The purpose of this work is to better characterise HF radar data for target detection.

articleTitle: Analysis of microstrip structures in multilayered substrates
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents an efficient technique for a full-wave analysis of microstrip antennas, circuits and discontinuities. The proposed method solves an electric field integral equation with mixed potentials and includes radiation and surface wave effects. Of paramount relevance is the accurate determination of dyadic Green's functions corresponding to the microstrip flat multilayered substrate. The integral equation is numerically solved with a method of moments featuring either subsectional or entire domain basis functions. Finally, a simple multiport analysis combined with a numerical de-embedding process allows the evaluation of equivalent circuits and/or scattering matrices independent of the excitation model used.

articleTitle: A feasibility study of small cassegrain antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A dual-band Cassegrain antenna system is recently proposed for use in the Space Station Freedom. The antenna is designed to operate in both S- and Ku-band frequencies. Design options include the use of a dichroic subreflector or a co-located dual-band feed horn. For mechanical simplicity, the dual-band feed option is chosen as a feasible design. The subreflector becomes electrically small at S-band (in the order of 3 wavelengths) and as a result the diffraction and the near-field effects have significant impact on the antenna performance. The paper reviews the accuracy of the Physical Optics method applied on small subreflectors and investigates experimentally the antenna loss due to the near-field effects. Comparison between computed and measured data on a scaled subreflector are discussed.

articleTitle: Coupled finite and boundary element methods in electromagnetic problems
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: As a general numerical technique for solving electromagnetic problems, the finite element method[FEM] appears to compete favorably with other numerical methods. As an example, when used for solving circuit discontinuities and EM scattering, it can handle arbitrarily shaped discontinuities, including anisotropic waveguide components such as ferrite devices. Various forms of FEM have been used in EM scattering problems. Usually the moment method is used, combined with various integral equations and equivalent techniques. One such technique is the newly developed hybrid finite element scheme[1] which overcomes the disadvantages of the unimoment method[2] by introducing two artificial boundaries. However, the inaccurate numerical derivatives are still involved as in the case of the unimoment method.

articleTitle: Frequency response measurements of the indoor channel
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes a novel method for the measurement of the frequency response of the indoor RF propagation channel utilizing an HP network analyzer. Preliminary measurements of the frequency response of the channel in the frequency bands 900–1000MHz and 1.6–1.8GHz are reported. These measurements determine the dependence of the rms excess delay time on the separation between the transmitting and receiving antennas, the propagation power law, the effect of antenna jiller on the received power level as well as the correlation bandwidth.

articleTitle: Propagation effects due to snow and melting particles along a propagation path
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Radio wave propagation characteristics in snow, wet ice and mixed phase hydrometeors along a propagation path are investigated. Included are further studies on differential propagation effects in snow, the melting region in stratiform precipitation, wet snow and ice on elevated paths. Results from radar measurements, at both linear and circular polarizations on elevated radar and satellite paths are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of circular patch antennas on electrically thick substrates
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Analysis of a probe fed circular patch antenna etched on electrically thick substrate is presented. The feed probe is considered to be the primary source of radiation, which induces currents on the patch surface. The patch is assumed to be a perfect conductor so that the tangential electric field is zero on the patch surface. The total reaction on the patch surface (sum of self reaction of the patch current and the mutual reaction between the patch current and the probe current) should therefore, be equal to zero. This condition is utilized to express the unknown patch current in terms of the probe current. The electromagnetic fields produced by the above currents are obtained employing the integral transformation technique [1]. The impedance seen by the probe feed is determined from the total reaction produced by the antenna and invoking the variational principle [2]. Numerical results for the input impedance, resonant frequency, bandwidth and radiation efficiency are obtained and found to vary widely with the normalized substrate thickness.

articleTitle: Analysis of phase center movement of linear phased array antenna-ground reflection effect
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A model for determining the antenna phase center and its movement due to multipath reception is defined and analyzed. It is shown that for the azimuth antenna in the Microwave Landing System (MLS) the phase center is susceptible to interaction of the direct signal and the indirect signals reflected by the ground.

articleTitle: RF filters and diplexers for cellular applications
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The conflicting requirements of continued cost reduction, miniaturization, higher transmit power and increased receiver sensitivity have made cellular radio diplexer design increasingly difficult. ‘Talk-time’, a measure of the quality of handheld cellular telephones, places the added burden of requiring minimum losses from these passive devices. Typically, RF filters account for over 10% of the volume of existing NovAtel radios. This paper covers the technology trends in diplexer filter components and describes the design methodology for ceramic resonator diplexers, currently in use in most cellular radios.

articleTitle: A novel solution to low-frequency problems with geometrically designed beamwaveguide systems
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The NASA Deep Space Network (DSN) is constructing a new 34-meter research and development antenna as a precursor to introducing beamwaveguide antennas and Ka-band frequencies into the operational network. The basic design of the center-fed beamwaveguide is shown in Figure 1. It consists of a beam magnifier ellipse in a pedestal room located below ground level that transforms a JPL standard 22-dB gain feedhorn into a high gain 29-dB gain pattern for input to a standard four-mirror (two flat and two paraboloid) beamwaveguide system.

articleTitle: Automatic focusing of an Applebaum array
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The effect of a finite distance of the signal source on the performance of an Applebaum array has been studied extensively in the literature. It has been concluded that unless the Applebaum Array is focused at the exact source location, the degradation of the output signal-to-noise ratio becomes unacceptable. The Automatic focusing technique (AFT) developed by the author for long wavelength imaging systems is used here to focus the Applebaum array at unknown source location. Thereafter, the far-field steering vector can be used successfully to form a beam towards the desired signal while suppressing the interference. In addition, substantial improvements in data processing have been achieved through the use of a partial convolution in the frequency domain. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that only half of the frequency spectrum can be used with negligible loss in signal-to-noise ratio and therefore, this procedure provides substantial reductions in data acquisition required by the AFT.

articleTitle: Theory and measurement for aperture coupled microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Interest in the use of microstrip patches for array antennas has prompted investigations into numerous feed mechanisms. One of the most interesting, which offers considerable advantages over the others, is aperture coupling. In the paper that follows, the coupling of a feedline to a rectangular patch, through an aperture in the ground plane separating them, is described. Modal field expansion is used to analyze the problem. The patch is described by the cavity model and the feedline is modeled as a transmission line. Coupling is assumed to be via a magnetic current in the aperture. Both theoretical and experimental design curves were generated and good agreement between them was obtained. Theoretical and experimental results were obtained for a single element antenna at 5 and 10 GHz respectively. This paper describes both theoretical and experimental results of work done to date.

articleTitle: Fields of a subsurface conductor buried in close proximity to the interface
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The determination of the propagation constants and fields for conductors embedded in a lossy half-space is of interest in low frequency radio transmission, remote sensing applications in geoelectromagnetics, and in the power engineering field for buried cable analysis. It is important to be able to determine the effect of the interface on the propagation and radiation characteristics of the geometry. In the past, almost all theories have treated the problem assuming a thin-wire approximation and/or a uniform axial current distribution to model the conductor. Under the thin-wire approximation, only axially directed currents with a uniform aztmuthal distribution are assumed. Under the uniform axial current assumption, there is no variation of the currents or fields in the axial dimension and thus only conduction currents in the earth are considered with displacement current effects being neglected. In this paper the validity of these approximations are examined by formulating the problem allowing for both an axial and azimuthal variation of the conductor currents. It is shown that for the bare buried conductor case, the accurate determination of the propagation constant is imperative for calculating the fields at the earth's surface. Further, it is shown that the thin-wire approximation is not valid for determining the fields in both the far and near field regions when the conductor is buried in close proximity to the interface. These results imply that the use of the thin-wire approximation and the uniform axial current assumption may not be valid for commonly occurring buried conductor problems.

articleTitle: Electro-optic measurement technique for millimetre wave antennas
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The development of high speed devices and materials for millimetre wave integrated antenna systems has sustained a need for ever faster and more flexible measurement systems. Several methods of performing time and frequency domain measurements of antenna near-field patterns and substrate electric fields exist using electro-optic sampling (EOS). An important feature of electro-optic sampling in antenna applications is its ability to directly measure the vector current distribution and mutual coupling effects on the antenna metallization. This technique promises to generate and measure pulses that have frequency ranges to the THz region, as compared with vector network analyzers that are limited to approximately 100 GHz and require electrical connections to the device being tested. We review electro-optic sampling techniques and their potential as a new “network analyzer” for the antenna engineer, enabling measurements to the 200 GHz range with a spatial resolution of micrometres. Initial experiments performed through a joint research program between the Ontario Laser Light Research Institute of Ontario (OLLRC) at the University of Toronto, and the Communications Research Laboratory (CRL) of McMaster University, are presented that demonstrate that the EOS technique is indeed a strong candidate for the measurement of millimetre wave antenna systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of slot-coupled double layer microstrip lines
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An analysis of slot-coupled double layer microstrip lines is presented. A modal field expansion method and the Poynting theorem are applied to derive the input impedance as seen by the feed line at the slot. By comparing the theoretical results with measured values, the accuracy of the method is verified.

articleTitle: A dual polarized X band microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A dual polarized microstrip patch array is being developed for use in a polarimetric synthetic aperture radar system. This paper presents an analysis and empirical results for the linear array in the elevation plane which will be replicated 96 times to form a 2.5m × 0.5m planar array. The vertical and horizontal polarizations of the linear array are series and aperture fed respectively. As a result of this feed arrangement the array exhibits exceptional polarization purity. Since the patches are resonant in both dimensions a degree of freedom is lost in the design of the series fed array. A procedure is presented for the series fed case which partially compensates this effect.

articleTitle: MLS angle antenna stability
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper contains an assessment of the stability of MLS angle antennas. The analysis contains a breakdown of the MLS angle error budget, from the system error to the ground equipment, environment, and propagation error sources. An assessment is made of MLS field data collected over a 12 month period from the Hazeltine Model 2600 MLS installed at the FAA Technical Center in Atlantic City, New Jersey. A statistical analysis is performed on the field data and a comparison is made to the ground equipment error budget allocation.

articleTitle: Accurate microstrip computation through minor refinements of the 3-D quasi-dynamic greens function
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The software EMsim™∗ has a graphical shell and a field theory “engine” WATMIC. This paper discusses the adjustments to the engine to improve the accuracy to 1 % error or less. The only limitation for new WATMIC is that it does not account for surface wave of substrates thicker than 0.05λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> (in the substrate).

articleTitle: Element response to an incident plane wave of a VHF circular array antenna above lossy ground
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A circular array receiving antenna is highly attractive for radio direction finding because of its geometrically circular symmetry and, thereby, the periodicity of its electromagnetic features, such as mutual coupling between elements of the array, when its beam is scanned electronically through 360 degrees. In radio direction finding systems, the elements of an array are considered to be sensors for the incoming wave. One of our principal concerns is the response of each element in the array to a plane wave. It will be treated as the input data vector for the digital signal processing system. The output voltage of an antenna element in a circular array, however, does not directly represent the amplitude and phase of the incident wave hitting the element antenna because of mutual coupling between the elements and the effect of lossy ground with a complex dielectric constant, ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>. In this paper, an analytical treatment and numerical results for the element response are provided. The discrete image theory and the method of moments are employed.

articleTitle: A reconfigurable L-band active array for satellite communications
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Design and experimental results of an L-band active array for mobile satellite communication antennas are presented in this paper. A receive feed array consisting of seven active modules is breadboarded. Each module consists of a circularly polarized radiating element, a stripline filter, a low-noise amplifier, a variable attenuator and a variable phase shifter. The output ports of the active modules are combined using a 7 to 1 beamforming network. Measured results of the septet array demonstrate that the beam shape can be reconfigured from 16° to 48° half-power beamwidth while the beam location can be reconfigured over ± 16° angular region. Low sidelobe and cross-polar levels have been maintained for the active array over the scan region.

articleTitle: Radiometric temperature for a coniferous forest at the microwave band
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In passive remote sensing techniques, the radiometric temperature emitted from a forested canopy is related to the canopy biophysical characteristics. In this study the radiative transfer theory is applied to study the radiometric temperature of a coniferous forest at the microwave band. The forest is modeled as layer above a rough soil surface. The layer is occupied by the leaves and the branches which are modeled as randomly oriented needles and finite-length cylinders respectively. Thermal emission sources are expressed in terms of the temperature profiles and the absorption coefficients of the scatterers within the layer. A perturbation technique is employed to solve the radiative transfer equations governing the radiometric temperature for such a medium. Both the zeroth and the first order solutions are obtained. Numerical results are presented to illustrate the relation between the radiometric temperature and the biophysical characteristics of the forest components (leaves and branches).

articleTitle: Transient response of circular cylinders a numerical approach
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The field transient response of a circular cylinder illuminated by a plane wave having a step function wave form in the time domain is computed using the Finite Difference-Time Domain (FD-TD) numerical technique. Both cases of conducting and dielectric circular cylinders are considered and correspondence between the transient response and the rise time of the excitation wave are investigated.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic induction response of metallic objects
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A simple model is used to explain spatial response characteristics of an electromagnetic induction detector as it scans over a metallic object. The technique is illustrated with numerical and experimental data for two mechanically identical prolate spheroids, one made of steel and the other of aluminium. Some basic differences in the response characteristics of a permeable and a non-permeable object are pointed out and explained.

articleTitle: Total field evaluation near the edge shadow of an idealized inflected surface
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The conventional Kouyoumjian transition function cannot be used to evaluate the diffracted field for a converging wave because its argument is imaginary, and the total field is not continuous at reflection and shadow boundaries. In order to find the diffracted field near the edge shadow of the inflected surface, Rusch's proposed edge-diffraction transition function for a converging wave is used. The argument of this transition function is real and it produces a continuous total field at the boundaries. The diffracted field is then added to the geometrical optics field and compared favorably with physical optics.

articleTitle: Modal current distributions on loop antennas in cylindrically stratified media
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper considers the modal current distribution on a loop antenna which is situated coaxially on the interface of a double-layered cylindrically stratified media. The loop is modelled as a Σ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n=1</inf>cos nφδ(z) electric current distribution under the influence of a unit amplitude rectangular voltage pulse function. The determination of the modal amplitudes of the current distribution follows an exact formalism employing Debye potentials. Numerical results illustrate the influence of the dielectric constant of the inner strata on modal current amplitude. These results suggest a method of modifying a loop antenna's radiation characteristics, which may be of benefit in certain applications.

articleTitle: The MMP codes: A 2D and 3D package implemented on PC's
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Generalized Multipole Technique is the base of the MMP (Multiple MultiPole) codes. This technique will be presented in the most simple and basic way with a brief historical introduction followed by the main principles. Then, the graphic editor and the structure of the codes will be presented, A short word on the implementation and parallelization of the codes will be given (INMOS Transputers, INTEL 80860). Finally, a paragraph will show the possibilities of combining the method with other well known methods (FEM, MoM, GTD).

articleTitle: Wideband components for advanced multi-function feed system
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Advanced multi-function Ku-band feed systems for satellite or earth station application require a number of operational features such as wide bandwidth, dual polarization, frequency reuse and polarization re-orientation. When built for satellite application, the feed system must also be compact, environmentally rugged and light weight. The realization of such a feed system calls for the development of some key components, viz., a half-wave polarizer, a rotary joint, an orthomode transducer and a diplexer. Successful development of the above components greatly depend on novel design concepts, precision electromagnetic field theory modelling, carefully defined fabrication procedure and extensive evaluation. This paper describes the technology base created for this class of components that has allowed an advanced multi-function feed system to be built and fully space qualified at COM DEV.

articleTitle: Accuracy of field computation in coaxial waveguides and cavities
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
