articleTitle: Ad Hoc development of a simple absorbing boundary for the FDTD method applied to rectangular waveguides
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents the development of a simple and effective plane absorbing boundary for the FDTD method. This absorbing boundary produces virtually no reflection at the tuning frequency, accomodates arbitrary incidence angle, and remains very local. The algorithm requires the knowledge of the field values at grid points lying only one space increment away from the absorbing boundary. The algorithm is based on ad hoc understanding of the wave propagation on a discrete mesh, with the concept of mesh, phase and group velocities. The efficacy of the absorbing boundary is demonstrated by measuring the reflection in the frequency domain for metallic rectangular waveguides operated in their dominant mode.

articleTitle: Static characteristics of a cylindrical microstrip line on a multilayered dielectric substrate partially embedded in a perfectly conducting ground plane
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The quasi-TEM characteristics of a microstrip line on a multilayered cylindrical dielectric substrate partially embedded in a perfectly conducting ground plane are rigorously determined. Exact expressions for the potential distributions inside and outside the substrate, charge distributions on the strip, and capacitance are derived.

articleTitle: Nonlinear modeling of GaAs FET parasitic resistances
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An analytical model for the parasitic resistance of MODFET's has been developed. The simulation results for the D.C. characteristics obtained when this model is used have been found to be in good agreement with the experimental data. This model shows that as the drain current, increases, the parasitic resistance increases which explains one of the effects responsible for the transconductance compression phenomenon in MODFET's. Using this parasitic resistance model improves the overall device model prediction, especially in high speed and microwave applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic reactive field imaging of printed circuit boards
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This article presents both theoretical and experimental aspects of the imaging of near fields of printed circuit boards (PCB). Selected aspects of sensor performance and imaging of reactive fields of simple PCB boards are also presented.

articleTitle: Compensation of antenna polarization cross-components by calibration
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The main objective of this article is to describe a calibration-based method for measuring the target backscattering matrix taking into consideration the cross-polarization error (distorsion) introduced by orthogonally polarized antennas used for transmission and recept ion.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of an arbitrarily fed insulated linear antenna in AIR
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Analytic expressions are derived for the input admittance and the current distribution along the arbitrarily-fed insulated antenna in air which is excited across a gap of non-zero width. In this work, the Wiener-Hopf type analysis for a center fed insulated antenna is extended to the case of asymmetrically excited antenna. Present analysis which does not employ superposition yields final expressions in terms of the excitation location as well as the aperture electric field within the gap. The results for the input admittance and current distribution are reported for different excitation location, outer radii and dielectric constants of the insulator at various antenna length.

articleTitle: Constraint propagation through electromagnetic interaction topologies
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The effects of electromagnetic interactions in electrical systems are of concern because of the increased pollution of the environment with electromagnetic emissions and because of the increasing susceptibility of system components. The term electrical system is used herein in the general sense to include more than just networks of electronic components. Systems containing biological and/or mechanical components of varying complexity are also included when reference to the term electrical systems is made. Electromagnetic emissions from components within the electrical system, and also disturbances originating external to it, can be classified as deriving from intentional as well as non-intentional sources. The interaction effects on the susceptible components within these systems range from minor to catastrophic; they cannot always be predicted nor are they always understood. Study and control of this problem is very desirable and has involved the efforts of many persons from varying fields.

articleTitle: Radiation from a lighted convex surface by means of Kottler's formula
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper Kottler's formula is extended to treat the radiation from a fictitious and enclosing convex regular surface of zero thickness where we know the electromagnetic field distribution at each point. When the product of the two main radius of curvature is lower than the square of the free space wavelength, the field calculated with Kottler's formula may be wrong. Acorrection term applied to the electromagnetic field components at each surface point means that a right radiated far field can be obtained by means of Kottler's formula.

articleTitle: On the MLS/ALS collocation
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The time reference scanning beam Microwave Landing System (MLS) is an air derived system, whereby airborne receivers decode continuous ground system data to provide guidance information indicating vertical and lateral displacement from a selected flight profile. It is expected that MLS, within ten years, will replace the Instrument Landing System (ILS) as a precision landing aids to aircrafts in most of the airports in Canada and worldwide.

articleTitle: Galerkin analysis OF F S S from circular apertures IM cunducting screen
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The frequency selective surfaces (FSS) find application in many diverse area, such as polarizers, antenna reflectors due to their resonance properties. In the case of infinite FSS are used: mode — matching method [1] and spectral — domain approach [2],[3]. For the infinite 20 periodical arrays is convenient to use the Floquet harmonics for the field representation in the free space.

articleTitle: TLM solution of general two dimensional scattering problems
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Transmission-Line Matrix (TLM) method, originated by Johns and Beurle [1] is based on equivalent circuit models of Maxwell's equations and has been used extensively to analyze electromagnetic field problems [2]. In this paper the application of the TLM method to two dimensional electromagnetic scattering problems is investigated. The configuration of the mesh is the same as that used in Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FD-TD) scattering simulations (i.e. separation of the simulation space into total and scattered field regions) [3]. To terminate the exterior boundaries of the mesh, absorbing boundary conditions are applied to absorb the outward travelling waves. Scattering by perfectly conducting rectangular and circular cylinders, and infinite arrays of strips is examined.

articleTitle: Microwave neural net-antenna array for electronic warfare systems
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microwave Neural Networks are introduced. These are microwave subsystems, designed on basis of the emerging Artificial Neural Network Theory, that together with inhomogenous antenna arrays, are able to perform identification tasks of radar emitters, in real time. A model is presented and its properties are commented. Considerations about the physical realization of such systems are given.

articleTitle: Time domain antenna measurements with HP8510 using Matrix Pencil method
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The HP 8510 Time Domain Network Measurements are actually frequency domain measurements transformed to time domain using Inverse Fourier Transform. This computational technique benefits from the wide dynamic range and the error correction of the frequency domain data. However, Inverse Fourier Transform requires frequency domain response measured over wide frequency range to give useful resolution in time domain. Use of Generalized Pencil-of-Function (GPOF) method, also known as Matrix Pencil method, as a means of transform from frequency to time domain will provide for much higher resolution. A comparison of two methods is given for the example of Beatty Standard.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic free oscillations in the presence of two conducting spheres
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: We consider the electromagnetic fields which can exist in the presence of two perfectly conducting spheres in free space in the absence of external sources, i.e. the free oscillations. An asymptotic analytical solution for the natural frequencies and natural modes is presented, which is exact in the limit of infinite sphere separation. To our knowledge this is the first analytical treatment of the free oscillations of a two-body geometry. The transcendental equation for the natural frequencies is solved numerically for a representative example. We examine the physical content, especially the feedback mechanism between the current on the two spheres which sustains the free oscillation (apart from radiation damping). This leads to the establishment of a physically logical link between a natural mode and its corresponding natural frequency.

articleTitle: Automated far-field antenna pattern measurement system for McMaster University's anechoic chamber
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An antenna pattern measurement system has been developed which operates over the frequency range 1 to 12.4 GHz. The system makes pattern measurements and tests gain, beamwidths, and sidelobe levels under far-field conditions. Measurements using a Hewlett-Packard 8410A vector network analyzer as the receiver are managed by an in-house-developed software package for use on an IBM PC-AT microcomputer.

articleTitle: The singular and bounded parts of dyadic Green's function in a rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A systematic derivation of singular and bounded parts of the electric and magnetic dyadic Green's functions of electric and magnetic current inside a rectangular waveguide using Poisson's summation formula is given in this paper. The rectangular waveguide of dimensions (a, b) is assumed to be oriented such that the “a” dimension is in the x-direction, and “b” dimension in the y-direction. Integrals of singular parts of these functions over rectangles arbitrarily oriented in the waveguide, useful in the computation of electric and magnetic fields in the source region of uniform distribution of electric and magnetic currents are also presented. Numerical results verifying the correctness and accuracy of these expressions are presented.

articleTitle: Integrated feed design for satellite communication antennas
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Satellite communication antennas commonly employ beamforming networks (BFN's) which hitherto have been realized with discrete components. This paper presents two alternative BFN technologies developed at Spar Aerospace, namely integrated waveguide and integrated TEM-line which advantageously replace the discrete component technology. The integrated feed concept is presented together with design examples of the new technologies at Ku-band and C-band. Measured results are also reported and comparison is made with discrete component BFN's of similar complexity.

articleTitle: An optimized impedance-matching technique for increasing the bandwidth of microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The usefulness of broadband impedance matching to increase the bandwidth of a microstrip patch antenna is illustrated using three different antenna configurations. Measured data for a patch antenna was incorporated into commercial CAD software to design a matching network. Design limitations are also discussed. Practical design examples and experimental results are given which clearly demonstrate the validity of this technique.

articleTitle: Future challenges in microstrip antennas and arrays
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: There are now many new microstrip antennas being produced in industrial centres throughout the world for a host of applications. However there still remains significant challenges in full exploitation of the unique capabilities of these printed antennas. Cost reduction and tolerance control to allow realistic mass production, exploitation of the conformal nature of microstrip and further integration with circuits are seen as just some of the factors currently facing designers. This paper reviews the current state of microstrip antenna technology and highlights significant future challenges in such important areas as innovation, analytic developments, computer aided design and manufacturing aspects.

articleTitle: A Least mean square error synthesis with pattern constraints at multiple frequencies
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The pattern synthesis technique described here is unique in that it allows the power pattern to be optimized in a very useful sense over the desired operating band of the array. This is an improvement over previous techniques involving constraints on such artificial parameters as source norm and superdirectivity ratio which do not in fact ensure a useful pattern bandwidth. The procedure described here provides minimum mean square error over an arbitrary number of discrete frequencies.

articleTitle: The use of 3D SCN-TLM method in computer-aided design of waveguide components
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The symmetrical condensed node (SCN) TLM method is used to compute S-parameters of various waveguide components. A discontinuous ridge waveguide, a resonant iris, a double plane waveguide transition and a symmetrical waveguide T-junction are analysed. The conditions which must be satisfied in the S-parameter computation of such circuits are defined. The validity of the method is verified by comparison with results obtained by experiment and other numerical methods. Very good agreement with those results has been achieved by virtue of the excellent wideband absorbing boundaries implemented in our method.

articleTitle: A tuneable elevated microstrip antenna for cellular handhelds
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Whip antennas can provide good performance for RF communications, such as cellular telephony, especially when mounted on top of vehicles. Unfortunately, they are not easily integrated into a small handheld chassis. As handheld radios become smaller and more ergonomic, the whip antenna represents a growing inconvenience to the user. This paper describes one member of a new family of antennas under development at NovAtel: Elevated Microstrip Antennas (EMAs). These can provide significant size and performance advantages yet are cost effective and readily manufactured. They combine high efficiency and controlled radiation characteristics in a compact and convenient geometry. Separation of the transmit and receive elements replaces much of the normal duplexer filtering function as well as reducing spurious interference. A significant advance is the capability of separately and actively tuning both the receive and transmit sections of EMAs. As in any radiating structure there are fundamental limitations constraining the practical size and performance of EMAs [1]. A specific implementation is presented along with a distributed passive element analysis, measured results, a discussion of compromises, and a 3D radiation plot from an automated antenna test range developed at NovAtel. It is concluded that EMAs are capable of providing performance equal to or better than a typical whip antenna but have several significant advantages.

articleTitle: RCS OF conducting cylinders with dielectric-filled cavities
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A problem of recent interest in electromagnetics is that of scattering from a conducting body with a dielectric-filled cavity. Other authors, [1]-[3], have investigated three-dimensional (3-D) bodies. Here we investigate scattering from two-dimensional (2-D) bodies (cylinders). Because it is a simpler case, results from the 2-D case are more easily interpreted.

articleTitle: Radar cross section of an array of dielectric spheres
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The normalized backscattering and bistatic cross sections for a linear array of N dielectric spheres are computed and presented graphically over wide ranges of permittivity, separation, size, and angle of incidence. The results show reduction in the normalized backscattering and bistatic cross sections for certain choices of permittivity relative to arrays of perfectly conducting spheres of same dimensions and separations.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling between stacked microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents some original results on mutual coupling between two identical stacked microstrip antennas. The mutual coupling is calculated by using the reciprocity theorem in the Spectral Domain. The theoretical results are in good agreement with experiments. As expected, we observe that the mutual coupling between stacked patches is stronger than that between unstacked patches.

articleTitle: Impedance variation of microstrip patch antenna with feedline width
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A theoretical and experimental study of the patch antenna input impedance variation with feedline width is presented. Measured results were compared with some of the currently available numerical models. A limitation of these numerical models was established and the techniques will be modified to overcome this shortcoming.

articleTitle: Large and small signal models for simulation of high speed modfet ICS
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Large and small signal models for GaAlAs MODFETs have been developed. Transconductances, conductances, and capacitances for the two dimensional electron gas (2DEG) and the AlGaAs parasitic layers have been formulated. The model was then implemented in SPICE.

articleTitle: Linearisation of a pin diode biphase attenuator
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes how a linear relationship between control voltage and transmission coefficient can be obtained for a PIN diode biphase attenuator. This linearisation comes out from a theoretical study of the attenuator. Results given here, are obtained for a microstrip biphase attenuator optimised at 1.59 GHz.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering from dielectric bodies of arbitrary shape
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A numerical method is presented to formulate the plane wave scattering from dielectric bodies of finite sizes. The formulations use the equivalence principle which casts the scattered field in terms of the unknown equivalent electric and magnetic currents. An application of the boundary conditions leads to a linear system of equations for the coefficients of the unknown currents. The resulted coupled integral equations are solved numerically by the method of moments. The procedure is applied to study the differential cross-section of geometries such as, dielectric spheres and finite cylinders, and cubes. An excellent agreement between the numerical results and the reported data is obtained.

articleTitle: Measurement of ocean wave spectra using a ship-mounted HF radar
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A data interpretation technique is presented and tested to extract the nondirectional ocean wave-height spectrum from the echo return of a ship-mounted HF radar employing an omnidirectional receive/transmit antenna. Tests of this technique at sea shows that there is a high degree of correlation between its wave spectra estimates and that of a WAVE-TRACK buoy.

articleTitle: A rigorous analysis of an aperture-coupled stacked microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A rigorous analysis of an aperture-coupled stacked microstrip antenna is described. Developed from a coupled integral equation set employing spectral-domain Green's functions, the analysis includes all coupling, radiation and surface-wave effects. Optimization of the patch dimensions yielded VSWR bandwidths of greater than 20%. Theoretical and measured responses exhibited excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Wire and aperture probe modeling in planar near-field scanning
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The use of planar near-field scanning is well developed in characterizing the far-field behavior of directive antennas<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup>. One of the important steps in predicting the far-field is the correction of the averaging effect introduced by the finite size of the probe used in the field measurement, and the methods of correction are well developed in this context<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2,3)</sup>. The existing formulation utilizes the complex radiation pattern of the probe as a basis for finding the radiation pattern of the antenna under test. This approach is useful when dealing with highly directive antennas and the resulting formulae are usually well-conditioned. However, there are cases when the antenna under test is nondirective or the near-field measurements are intended to collect data for an inverse problem. It is, then, important to investigate the behavior of the field probes for general incident fields.

articleTitle: Modelling printed circuit applicators for biomedical applications
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: We propose to investigate printed circuit applicators for biomedical applications: the microstrip-microslot and the microstrip applicators laid on multilayered lossy media and covered or not with a superstrate. We want to get their fundamental characteristic parameters: the complex propagation constant (relative effective permittivity ∊<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">reff</inf>, attenuation α), the associated characteristic impedance Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> and more particularly the power penetration inside biological tissues (electric field distribution, depth penetration and heating pattern). This analysis is based on the Spectral Domain Approach (S.D.A.) method.

articleTitle: Incorporation of edge conditions in scattering from conducting objects of finite sizes
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The use of an edge condition in scattering problems is investigated. Various numerical schemes such as conformal transformation, Fourier expansion, and Fourier expansion with edge correction are examined. The developed numerical methods are then applied to investigate the dynamic range of each techniques and their validity.

articleTitle: A curled slot antenna adopting a triplate configuration
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: We have proposed and discussed a dual-spiral slot as a circularly polarized radiation element with a simple feeding system [1]. The dual-spiral slot located in the x-y plane, as shown in Fig. 1(a), has different radiation patterns in the x-z and y-z planes, due to its dual-element configuration. When the same radiation pattern is required in the x-z and y-z planes, the dual configuration is changed to a single element configuration, as shown in Fig. 1(b).

articleTitle: Multiport network modeling of electro magnetically coupled microstrip patches
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Electromagnetically coupled (EM fed) microstrip patches have their feed structure fabricated on a thin substrate located between the patch antenna and its ground plane as shown in Figure 1. This dual layer design has two main advantages over conventional single layer microstrip antennas. First, spurious radiation from the feed network can be reduced by decreasing the height and increasing the dielectric constant of the lower substrate. Secondly, patch bandwidth can be increased by using a thicker upper dielectric material and also by adjusting the feed configuration under the patch. Previous methods of designing EM fed patches have included experimental iteration, transmission line model [1], and full wave analysis [2] [3]. Unfortunately, experimental iteration is time consuming and costly; the transmission line model only works for feeds under the radiating edge of the patch; and full wave analysis is computationally intensive.

articleTitle: Boundary element method analysis of MIC devices
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A new model for analyzing discontinuities in MIC devices is being proposed. The technique is based on the boundary element method. An MIC device with an arbitrarily shaped discontinuity can be treated as a one-dimensional problem. Two numerical examples are given for checking the validity of the model.

articleTitle: Mutual impedance between two air-dielectric microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A moment method solution for the Electric Field Integral Equation is used to analyse a rectangular patch air-dielectric microstrip antenna on an infinite size ground plane. The patch surface is modelled by surface patch modes. The mutual impedance between the surface patch modes are calculated using a simple formula. The effect of the fringing field at the edges of the rectangular patch is derived and added to the moment method solution. The input impedance for an isolated element and the mutual impedance between two antennas are calculated.

articleTitle: An efficient technique for the analysis of microstrip circuits and antennas
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The objective of this paper is to present a numerical technique for the analysis of printed circuits and antennas using the grounded dielectric slab Green's functions. For the dynamic case, the Green's functions are quite complicated and require the numerical computation of certain semi-infinite integrals commonly known as the Sommerfeld integrals. In this paper certain approximations have been made resulting in much simpler expressions for the near field Green's functions. Finally, numerical examples are presented in order to validate the technique.

articleTitle: MOM analysis of a cavity-FED shaped beam reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Shaped beam reflector antennas are commonly used in satellite communications applications where performance considerations other than high gain may be of importance. For large antennas, the feed and reflector are usually considered to be uncoupled and are analysed separately [1]. The analysis of the feed requires a more exact solution technique with an integral equation formulation or mode expansion method usually being employed. Once this is accomplished, the geometrical theory of diffraction can then be used to analyse the reflector with the specified feed illumination ignoring their interaction. However, for antennas where the reflector size or its separation from the feed is not large compared to the free space wavelength, the coupling between the feed and reflector can not be ignored. This paper examines the use of the integral equation formulation approach for analysing rotationally symmetric reflector antennas whose diameter is on the order of tens of wavelengths. In this case the entire feed and reflector structure are modeled in the integral equation and thus are fully coupled. The specific example that will be considered is the European Space Agency telemetry antenna for the ERS-1 radarsat satellite. This antenna has been examined extensively in the literature, with published experimental radiation pattern results being available for comparison to the numerical solution.

articleTitle: Antenna design for a multifrequency imaging microwave radiometer
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A mechanically-scanned offset reflector with a multiple feed array is proposed as a feasible configuration for a radiometric antenna. The antenna is designed to operate over six different frequency bands, ranging from 6.80 GHz to 90.0 GHz, and is optimized to simultaneously satisfy the requirements on beam footprint overlap, sidelobe and cross-polar levels. Computed electrical performance is presented for all the frequency bands.

articleTitle: Design of a printed annular-slot array generating circularly polarized conical patterns
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A land-mobile or a maritime antenna for local-area satellite ccmmunications of relatively low G/T can be realized by using a circularly polarized antenna generating a conical pattern. Because of its omnidirectional pattern in a horizontal plane and fairly wide beamwidth in a vertical plane, there is almost no need for tracking the satellite.

articleTitle: An application of stochastic system identification to geo-electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Concepts from modern system identification theory have been applied to the processing of stochastic electromagnetic (EM) signals of geophysical origin in order to separate a desired signal from corrupting background noise for situations where a priori knowledge of the noise statistics is minimal. Parametric identification has been utilized in controlled source electromagnetic methods (CSEM) for the separation of the target signal from the noise (viz., natural fields and geological and topographic noise) by using only information provided by the received signal measured at a base sensor and by the reference inputs measured at the remote or reference sensors. A recursive maximum-likelihood prediction-error algorithm, which permits data processing in either an off-line or an on-line, real-time mode, has been implemented and applied to both synthetic and real CSEM data in order to demonstrate the potential value of the method developed.

articleTitle: A comparison of CAD models for the radiation from a rectangular microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Different radiation formulas are compared for the case of a rectangular microstrip patch antenna, either on an infinite substrate (Fig. la) or on an infinite ground plane with the substrate truncated at the boundary of the patch (Fig. lb). For both the infinite and truncated substrate cases the electric current model is compared with the magnetic current model using the dominant-mode assumption. A more exact radiation model is then developed which accounts for radiation from the probe and higher-order modes, and this is compared with the simpler dominant-mode models. A comparison will also made with measured results.

articleTitle: Moment method analysis of parallel plate EMP simulators made from two sets of parallel wires
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Parallel plate EMP simulators can be made from two sets of parallel wires to reduce wind loading, weight, and icing problems. The available literature on this kind of simulator construction is inadequate for the prediction of such basic design information as characteristic impedance and field enhancement.

articleTitle: L-band integrated feed array design for mobile communication satellite
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The space segment of a mobile satellite communication system must provide high power densities (EIRP) on the ground to allow mobiles with small low gain antennas to communicate. With the emerging high power multiple channel mobile communication satellites, the interference caused by Passive Intermodulation (PIM) is now recognized as an important spacecraft performance parameter. Several antenna concepts were evaluated for mobile satellite applications. Multiple beam reflectors were found to give best overall performance. Significant design efforts and breadboard activities resulted in the development of a primary feed array suitable for mobile satellite applications. This paper presents the integrated design approach which has been selected to minimize the risk of interference caused by PIM. Each radiator element consists of a cup dipole integrated with an output bandpass filter. The paper describes the radiating element and the associated filter design together with the detailed cup/filter interface. Presented also are the measured test results of the developed hardware.

articleTitle: Application of cubic phase theory to Galindo-Williams subreflector
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A JPL Fortran program for designing the main reflector and the subreflector of a Galindo-Williams system with a constant intensity over the aperture of the main reflector was modified for use on our computer system. Geometrical Optics and conservation of energy are the basic laws used for designing this type of surface. The basic computation is a numerical solution of three simultaneous differential equations. The resulting subreflector is a type of inflected surface. Analysis of the fields scattered from such surface using physical optics yields adequate results. Cubic-phase theory is numerically applied to the Galindo-Williams surface. Although the technique appeared to yield results accurate to within 1015%, the near-ness of the edge to the turning point caused a coupling of the edge and turning point solutions, which prevented higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Radar backscattering from vegetation targets
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: For remote sensing of forests, knowledge of the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of tree leaves, branches and trunks is important. Various theoretical models based on the analytic solution of the Helmholtz integral have been developed for tree components. The trunks, branches, stems and coniferous leaves are treated as lossy dielectric cylinders. The deciduous leaves are treated as elliptic discs. The ultimate check on the validity of any model is its simplicity and how close it approximates the experimental results. In the present investigation we present some actual experimental results from measurements performed on tree branches and leaves along with theoretical results. The samples measured represent various sizes and shapes of branches and leaves. Obviously, it will not be practical to measure various possible combinations, but our aim is to use some of the limited, but accurate, data to provide confidence in the theoretical modeling.

articleTitle: The effects of rain on microwave landing system antenna radomes
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Testing has indicated the sensitivity of the performance of Microwave Landing System antennas to the presence of water on the antenna radomes. Effects include degradation of system accuracy, effective radiated power, and system monitoring. Research has also been conducted in an attempt to find suitable radome materials with water shedding (hydrophobic) properties that would eliminate the problem. Test results and a discussion of candidate radome materials are presented.

articleTitle: Approximate modeling of scattering by systems of coaxial prolate spheroids
publicationTitle: 1990 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, an approximate method is described for solving the problem of electromagnetic scattering by two coaxial prolate spheroids, with their major axes along the common axis. The incident wave is considered to be a monochromatic uniform plane electromagnetic wave of arbitrary polarization, and angle of incidence. The method is based on the exact solution to scattering of a plane wave by a single spheroid. To account for the multiple interactions between the spheroids, the total field seen by each spheroid is written as the sum of the fields corresponding to the incident plane wave and to another plane wave of unknown magnitude propagating along the common axis from the other spheroid. Thus the total far field scattered by each spheroid can be written as the sum of the field scattered due to the incident plane wave and the field scattered due to the plane wave of unknown magnitude, propagating axially. The total far field scattered by one spheroid can also be written as the sum of the field scattered by that spheroid due to the incident plane wave and the field scattered due to the total far field scattered by the other spheroid, acting as an incident plane wave on the first spheroid. Equating the two different expressions of the total far field scattered by each of the spheroids, corresponding to transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarizations separately, yields a set of simultaneous linear equations, whose solution gives finally the total far scattered field at any given point in space.
